# Spec-Kit Studio

> Spec-Kit Studio is an open-source, local-first workspace for reviewable specification-driven delivery with GitHub Spec Kit and optional coding agents.

Canonical project page: https://rraviku2-uhg.github.io/spec-kit-studio/
Source repository: https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio
License: Apache-2.0
Current version: 0.1.20

## Product

- [Project overview](https://rraviku2-uhg.github.io/spec-kit-studio/): Purpose, workflow, trust boundaries, and documentation.
- [README](https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio#readme): Capabilities, supported platforms, setup, and operational boundaries.
- [Getting started](https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio/wiki/Getting-Started): Installation on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): Browser, server, connector, storage, and integration architecture.
- [Security](https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Vulnerability reporting and trust boundaries.

## Key facts

- Studio connects requirements, accepted persona evidence, reviewed engine artifacts, isolated worktree execution, verification receipts, and handoff evidence.
- Local repository access is performed by an optional loopback connector restricted to configured roots.
- Consequential actions require explicit operator confirmation; generated output is never treated as approved automatically.
- The application supports Node.js 22 on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Studio can generate portable prompts for Codex, Claude, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini, and Cursor.
- GitHub Spec Kit v1.0.6 is the only verified strict engine adapter. Other selectable engine profiles are future-facing and do not yet provide CLI lifecycle support.
- Available personas are Product Manager, Business Analyst, Developer/Architect, and Security Researcher; their accepted artifacts are reused only through declared, feature-scoped consumption rules.
- A completed developer handoff separates strict engine artifacts, Studio review evidence, and repository code. After a developer commits and pushes a clean linked-worktree branch, they may explicitly create a GitHub PR through their local `gh` session; Studio retains the resulting PR record in delivery evidence but never commits, pushes, merges, or deploys.
- GovCloud and DoD modes are fail-closed deployment postures. When active, Studio shows a persistent boundary banner; this is not a certification or authorization claim.
